raw:
{
  "question_intent": "Sustainability of AI roles in the UK and US, and potential risks for the UK.",
  "main_topics": ["AI roles in the UK and US", "sustainability", "potential risks for the UK", "disruptive mindset", "primary banking relationships", "customer service", "digital transformation"],
  "answer_completeness": "Complete",
  "response_stance": "Mixed",
  "evidence_level": "Medium",
  "contains_numeric_evidence": false,
  "contains_forward_guidance": false,
  "narrative_alignment": "Partially aligned",
  "question_quote": "At the beginning of the remarks, you mentioned UK is more of an incumbent in terms of AI, while in the US, it's more of a disruptor. So, if we're thinking further down the line, which one of the two parts is the most sustainable in that regard. You're thinking being in the US as a disruptor makes sense, would that open risks for the UK from potential disruptors?",
  "answer_quote": "Good question. Thank you. We do think of ourselves on either side of the Atlantic, certainly in retail terms as different things. And originally started as the card business in the US, but now what you've seen is us adding a digital savings platform and now digital unsecured lending. So, pulling that together and being very partner-focused with a broad representation. So, it's not a bricks-and-mortar business. Interestingly, and I don't think we talk about this so much, bigger than Chase in the UK. It's a substantial business. And we do see opportunities to grow it with that sort of framework in mind. So very digitally led. In the UK, we start from a very different place. In UK Corporate or in Barclays UK, you're talking about very, very strong primary banking relationships, which, as you say, is where I started this discussion. So, you're really trying to bring your customer or your client into your ecosystem and do as much for them as possible. That's very different from the kind of disruptive mindset. We see our strategy from here as being very much a continuation of that. That said, in the UK, it's really important that the app and the pricing are as good as those of our competitors and indeed our customer service. We've made a lot of progress over the last few years. We're now pretty much top of the large banks in terms of customer service, but we don't recognise that as the standard that we need to get to because of some of the disruptors around us. I think of it as remaining true to being a disruptor in the US and in the UK using the disruptive elements around you to make your primary relationship better and better and better."
}
